github-actions.notes: Add .gitattributes check as first step in CI job.

core.description: Enforce line endings at the Git layer using .gitattributes. Mark text files with appropriate EOL handling (eol=lf for shell scripts, eol=auto for most files) and binary files as binary to prevent corruption. This prevents 'works locally, fails in CI' issues caused by CRLF/LF mismatches.
core.label: Git Attributes (Line Endings)

machineCheck.description: Verify no CRLF in shell/script files

stack.notes: Use .gitattributes as the authority for EOL; .editorconfig is supplementary for editor display. Mark *.sh, *.bash as eol=lf. After adding .gitattributes, run 'git add --renormalize .' to fix existing files. Windows contributors should set core.autocrlf=false and core.safecrlf=warn (safecrlf=true blocks normalization with fatal errors).
stack.verification: Run 'git ls-files --eol' and verify no unexpected CRLF in LF-only files.

github-actions.notes: Add CRLF detection step before main CI steps.

core.description: Fail CI early for Linux-executed files containing CRLF line endings. Shell scripts, Python files, and other interpreted files fail silently or with cryptic errors when they contain \r characters. Detect this before running deeper CI steps.
core.label: CRLF Detection in CI

stack.notes: Check for CRLF in .sh, .js, .ts, .json files early in CI. Use 'file' command or grep for \r to detect issues before they cause cryptic failures.
stack.verification: Run 'git ls-files --eol | grep w/crlf' and verify no unexpected CRLF files.

core.description: Maintain proper .gitignore and .dockerignore files to prevent committing secrets, build artifacts, or unnecessary files.
core.label: Git and Docker Ignore Files

stack.notes: Use the official github/gitignore Node template as a base and add .env*, node_modules, dist/, coverage/, *.log, npm-debug.log*, etc. .dockerignore must exclude node_modules, .git, and local build output.
stack.verification: .gitignore must exist; .dockerignore is recommended when containerizing or using Docker workflows.

core.description: Run static code linting to enforce consistency and catch common issues early.
core.label: Linting

bazelHints.notes: Example only; actual targets are repo-defined. Wrap eslint via aspect_rules_lint or a custom sh_test rule.

stack.notes: Treat new lint errors as CI failures; keep existing issues as warnings until addressed.
stack.verification: Presence of eslint.config.js (or any .eslintrc* file) indicates linting is enforced for the repository.

core.description: Provide a deterministic unit test framework with a single command to run all tests.
core.label: Unit Test Runner

bazelHints.notes: Bazel discovers and runs all test targets. Use rules_js for Jest/Vitest integration.

stack.notes: Keep unit tests fast and deterministic; move slow or flaky tests into integration or E2E suites.
stack.verification: Test framework configuration is present; test script is defined in package.json.

core.description: Provide a Dockerfile and, if applicable, a docker-compose file for local dev and CI parity.

stack.notes: Use multi-stage builds and pin Node.js and base image versions in the Dockerfile to match CI (e.g., node:22-alpine).
stack.verification: Dockerfile must be present; docker-compose.yml is optional and indicates orchestration usage.

core.description: Use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versioning with clear rules and automated changelog generation based on commit history. Maintain a single canonical version source (for example, package.json or VERSION) that all release artifacts use.
core.label: Semantic Versioning

stack.notes: Automate version bumping and changelog generation from Conventional Commits using semantic-release or standard-version. Keep package.json (or a VERSION file) as the single canonical version source and have CI publish npm/GitHub/Docker artifacts from that same version. Protect release branches and ensure release tooling only runs there.
stack.verification: Check that the canonical version field follows SemVer, and trigger the configured release workflow (for example, a dry run of semantic-release or standard-version) to confirm it generates the expected next version, updates package.json or VERSION, and creates/updates CHANGELOG.md with commit-based entries.

github-actions.notes: Run the version guard in PR workflows against the base ref.

core.description: If semantic-release or automated versioning is enabled, block manual edits to canonical version fields in pull requests. Enforce a CI guard (and optional pre-push hook) that fails when version lines change outside the release workflow.
core.label: Version Guard (Automated Releases)

stack.notes: Add a CI step that runs scripts/check-version-unchanged.sh against the PR base ref. This blocks manual edits to package.json version when semantic-release owns versioning. Optionally wire the same script into a pre-push hook for fast feedback.
stack.verification: Run the guard with the PR base ref (for example, origin/main) and confirm it fails when package.json version changes.

github-actions.notes: Ensure format:check step uses ignore file that excludes release artifacts.

core.description: Exclude auto-generated release artifacts (CHANGELOG.md, package-lock.json, etc.) from code formatters to prevent CI failures. Release automation tools generate files that may not conform to your formatter's style, causing format checks to fail on subsequent CI runs.
core.label: Release Artifact Formatter Exclusion

stack.notes: Add CHANGELOG.md and package-lock.json to .prettierignore. These files are auto-generated by semantic-release and npm respectively. Without this exclusion, format:check fails after releases because the generated format differs from Prettier's expected style. Document each exclusion with a comment explaining it's auto-generated.
stack.verification: Run 'npm run format:check' and confirm CHANGELOG.md is not checked. Review .prettierignore and confirm auto-generated files are listed with explanatory comments.

core.description: Use a single CI release pipeline that publishes all artifacts (GitHub releases, packages, containers) from the same canonical version source.
core.label: Unified Release Workflow

stack.notes: Release workflow must publish npm packages, GitHub releases, and Docker images from the same canonical version (package.json or VERSION). Avoid separate manual steps or ad-hoc scripts for different artifacts.
stack.verification: Trigger the release pipeline and confirm all artifacts share the same version number and tag.

github-actions.notes: Set HUSKY=0 or equivalent in release job to disable hooks.

core.description: Release automation must bypass local developer hooks (HUSKY=0, --no-verify) and rely solely on CI gates for validation. This ensures idempotent, reproducible releases that don't fail due to hook environment differences.
core.label: Release Hook Bypass

machineCheck.command: grep -r 'HUSKY=0\|--no-verify' .github/workflows/ || echo 'WARNING: No hook bypass in release workflow'

stack.notes: In release workflows, set HUSKY=0 environment variable to disable husky hooks. Release commits from semantic-release should bypass commitlint since they're generated. CI gates already validated the code.
stack.verification: Check release workflow for HUSKY=0 or --no-verify flags.

core.description: Enforce structured commit messages such as Conventional Commits via commit-msg hooks and CI. This is required for deterministic versioning and changelog generation.
core.label: Commit Linting

stack.notes: Enforce Conventional Commits via commit-msg hooks (e.g., Husky) and a CI job so versioning/changelog automation is deterministic.
stack.verification: Create a test commit using the documented convention and ensure the commit message passes both local commit-msg hooks and CI checks.

core.description: Generate readable unit test and coverage reports and enforce a minimum coverage threshold (around 80%) for new or changed code.

bazelHints.notes: Bazel coverage collects coverage data from all test targets. Use --combined_report=lcov for aggregated reports.

stack.notes: Collect coverage in lcov or similar format; use diff coverage so legacy gaps are visible but non-blocking.
stack.verification: Run the unit tests with coverage enabled and confirm that a coverage report is produced and that the configured threshold (around 80%) is enforced for new changes.

core.description: Single CI pipeline that runs linting, formatting, type checking, tests, coverage, build, and containerization.
core.label: CI Quality Gates

bazelHints.notes: Replace npm run ci with Bazel commands. All quality gates run as Bazel targets.

stack.notes: Expose a single npm script (e.g., `npm run ci`) that mirrors the CI pipeline so contributors can reproduce failures locally.
stack.verification: Open the CI configuration and verify there is a job or stage that runs linting, type checking, tests, build, and any required container checks before merging to main.

core.description: Automatic code formatting to maintain a consistent style across all contributors.
core.label: Code Formatter

bazelHints.notes: Wrap Prettier as a run target for formatting checks. Use aspect_rules_lint for format aspects.

stack.notes: Run Prettier in check mode in CI; auto-fix locally via pre-commit hooks or editor integration.
stack.verification: Run the formatter in check mode (for example, `npm run format:check`) and confirm it reports clean formatting on committed code and auto-fixes as expected locally.

github-actions.notes: Hooks and CI must invoke identical verification commands. Use npm run verify or equivalent.

core.description: Use git hooks to run linting, formatting, and commit linting before changes are committed. Hooks should CHECK by default (not auto-fix), be fast, and scope to changed files only. Use a single entry hook mechanism (e.g., Husky as entry point calling pre-commit or lint-staged).
core.label: Pre-Commit Hooks

stack.notes: Use Husky as the entry hook mechanism calling lint-staged. Hooks should CHECK (--check flags) not auto-fix to keep developers aware of issues. Scope to staged files only for speed. Invoke hooks through the repo toolchain (npx) not global installs to ensure environment pinning. Never let hook enforcement drift from CI.
stack.verification: Run 'npm run verify' (or equivalent) and confirm the same checks run in both hooks and CI.

github-actions.notes: CI should call the same verify script that hooks use locally.

core.description: Local hooks and CI must invoke identical verification commands to prevent 'works locally, fails in CI' issues. Use a single canonical verify entrypoint (e.g., npm run verify) that both hooks and CI call.
core.label: Hook/CI Parity

stack.notes: Define a 'verify' script in package.json that runs all checks (lint, format:check, typecheck). Both .husky/pre-commit and CI should call 'npm run verify'. Never add checks to CI that don't run locally.
stack.verification: Compare hook commands with CI commands and confirm they invoke the same scripts.

github-actions.notes: Enable GitHub secret scanning and also run gitleaks in CI.

core.description: Scan staged diffs for credentials, API keys, and secrets before they reach the remote repository. Catch secrets at commit time rather than after they're pushed.
core.label: Pre-commit Secret Scanning

stack.notes: Add gitleaks or detect-secrets to pre-commit hooks. Scan only staged changes for speed. Configure allowlists for false positives in .gitleaks.toml.
stack.verification: Run 'gitleaks protect --staged' and verify it catches test secrets.

core.description: Use static type checking to catch errors before runtime and enforce strictness on new code. For JS/TS stacks, require a TypeScript-first policy with strict mode and a CI typecheck step; allow JSDoc/checkJs migration for legacy JS.
core.label: Type Checking

bazelHints.notes: TypeScript type errors surface during bazel build with rules_ts. No separate typecheck step needed.

stack.notes: Adopt a TypeScript-first policy. Require tsconfig.json with strict mode enabled ('strict': true) and enforce `npm run typecheck` (or equivalent) in CI. For legacy JS, allow JSDoc + `checkJs` or staged migration with `allowJs` while incrementally increasing coverage.
stack.verification: tsconfig.json exists with strict mode enabled and CI runs the typecheck script; legacy JS modules use JSDoc/checkJs or allowJs as an explicit migration path.

core.description: Lock dependencies and scan regularly for known vulnerabilities; fail CI on newly introduced high-severity issues.
core.label: Dependency Management & Vulnerability Scanning

stack.notes: Require a lockfile for reproducible installs and pin Node.js/tooling versions; block merges on new high-severity vulnerabilities.
stack.verification: Dependency lockfile is present; security scanning is configured in CI or project tooling.

core.description: Ensure builds are reproducible by pinning dependencies, base images, and tool/runtime versions. Avoid network/time variance and fail when lockfiles drift.
core.label: Deterministic & Hermetic Builds

stack.notes: Require a lockfile and pinned Node/tool versions (.nvmrc or .tool-versions). Pin base images in Dockerfiles and avoid non-deterministic install flags.
stack.verification: Lockfile is present and CI uses a frozen/immutable install. Dockerfiles reference pinned base images.

core.description: Produce SBOMs or provenance metadata, enable secret/code scanning, and sign tags or commits for critical repos.

stack.notes: Generate SBOM/provenance for npm and container artifacts, enable secret scanning, and sign tags/commits for protected branches.
stack.verification: SBOM/provenance artifacts are published alongside releases, and CI runs secret/code scanning.

core.description: Adopt standard CI templates and config samples to scale across repositories, minimizing bespoke pipeline logic.

stack.notes: Use shared CI templates for lint/test/build/release stages and keep repo-specific overrides minimal.
stack.verification: CI pipeline references a shared template or reusable workflow and follows the standard job naming.

core.description: Specify required runtime/engine versions in package manifests appropriate for your application. Use minimum version constraints (>=) rather than strict ranges to avoid blocking consumers from upgrading.
core.label: Runtime Version Specification

stack.notes: Specify the 'engines' field in package.json with a minimum version appropriate for your application (e.g., "engines": { "node": ">=20" }). Use open-ended constraints (>=) to avoid blocking consumers from upgrading. Only use upper bounds (<) when there are known incompatibilities.
stack.verification: package.json must contain an 'engines' field specifying the minimum required Node.js version.

core.description: Maintain a comprehensive README and, where applicable, auto-generated API docs to support onboarding and maintainability.

stack.notes: README should describe setup, scripts, and architecture; generate API docs from TypeScript types and JSDoc where helpful.
stack.verification: README.md is present in the repository root; docs/ directory or documentation tooling configuration exists if applicable.

core.description: Include standard governance files (LICENSE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md), branch protection rules, and review standards to define legal, ethical, and workflow expectations.
core.label: Repository Governance

stack.notes: Use an SPDX license identifier in package.json and describe review expectations, tests, and docs requirements in CONTRIBUTING.md.
stack.verification: LICENSE file is present in the repository root; CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and CONTRIBUTING.md are present for contribution guidance.

github-actions.notes: CI should call the canonical verify command, not duplicate check logic.

core.description: Provide one canonical 'verify' command per repository/stack that all stages call with appropriate flags. This prevents duplication, drift, and ensures consistency between local development and CI.
core.label: Canonical Verify Entrypoint

stack.notes: Define 'npm run verify' that runs lint, format:check, typecheck, and test. Pre-commit hooks call 'npm run verify:quick' (lint + format only). CI calls 'npm run verify' (full suite). Never duplicate verification logic across multiple scripts.
stack.verification: package.json contains a 'verify' script that orchestrates all checks.

github-actions.notes: Ensure CI reads from authoritative configs, not duplicated settings.

core.description: Each configuration rule must live in exactly one authoritative config file. Avoid duplication across .editorconfig, linter configs, and CI definitions. Document which file is authoritative for each concern.
core.label: Config File Authority Rules

stack.notes: Authority mapping: .gitattributes for EOL (Git layer), .editorconfig for editor display, eslint.config.js for lint rules, tsconfig.json for TS compiler options, prettier for formatting. Never duplicate rules across files.
stack.verification: Review configs and confirm no rule is defined in multiple places with potential for drift.

github-actions.notes: CI should read skip paths from config files, not hardcode them in pipeline.

core.description: Encode path exclusions and skip rules deterministically in config files, not through ad-hoc human judgment. Make it clear which paths are excluded from checks and why.
core.label: Explicit Skip Paths

stack.notes: Define ignores in eslint.config.js (ignores array) and .prettierignore. Document why each path is excluded (generated code, vendor, etc.). Avoid ad-hoc --ignore-path flags in scripts.
stack.verification: Review ignore configs and confirm all exclusions are documented and intentional.

core.description: Three-value exit-code contract shared across all hook scripts and CI preflight runners: 1 = quality regression (fatal), 2 = missing tool (fatal, setup issue), 3 = network or infra degraded (skippable with --allow-local-degraded). Inconsistent exit semantics across hooks mask real failures and undermine local/CI parity.
core.label: Hook Exit-Code Contract

optionalEnhancements.description: Standardize error handling and structured logging to make debugging and production monitoring easier.

Lock scope to identifier presence only — never prose, row counts, or link shapes — or the test devolves into churn-bait. Must include adversarial negative tests proving it catches fabricated and removed gates.
recommended.label: Parity Doc Coverage Test

recommended.description: Hook checks organize into three tiers: pre-commit (staged-only, fast), pre-push (CI-identical preflight superset), CI (remote-only jobs). Makes the local/CI boundary explicit and keeps fast-feedback checks from drifting toward either extreme.
recommended.label: Tiered Hook Model

recommended.description: Single entrypoint script that husky hooks delegate to. Routes pre-commit / pre-push / commit-msg based on argv, centralizes exit-code handling, tool detection, and network-degraded behavior so individual hook files stay thin and consistent.
recommended.label: Hook Dispatcher Script

recommended.description: Dedicated script that runs the CI-identical superset of gates. Pre-push hook invokes it; CI can also invoke it. Keeps local and CI verification paths mechanically equivalent rather than merely 'similar.'
recommended.label: Pre-Push Preflight Script

recommended.description: Hook scripts verify prerequisites upfront — .husky/ present, required tools on PATH, harness wired — and fail with a setup-specific exit code when any are missing. Prevents silent hook bypass after bad installs, branch switches, or dependency drift.
recommended.label: Fail-Fast Hook Setup Check

recommended.description: Static test asserting every table declared in the canonical schema source is either in a 'fundamental' set (present since inception) or created by at least one registered migration. Shifts detection of 'added table to schema, forgot the migration' from production runtime to PR CI.
recommended.label: Schema/Migration Parity Test

recommended.description: PRAGMA/DDL byte-equivalence test between (a) the canonical schema source and (b) a DB built by running every registered migration against a blank start. Catches semantic drift between inline schema and incremental migrations.
recommended.label: Migration DDL Byte-Parity

recommended.description: At DB connect time, validate table presence in two phases — 'fundamental' tables before any migrations run, 'required' tables after all migrations apply. Defense-in-depth alongside the parity test; catches the same defect class at runtime if it escapes PR gating.
recommended.label: Required-Tables Runtime Check

recommended.description: CI gate asserting the schema_version seed in the canonical schema source equals max(target_version) across all registered migrations. Catches 'added migration, forgot to bump seed' — where the DB migrates to v7 but schema source still claims v6.
recommended.label: Schema Version Seed Monotonic

recommended.description: Every registered migration has at least one test exercising it on a blank DB AND on the prior schema version. Enforced by a coverage check over the migration registry. Blocks untested migrations from shipping.
recommended.label: Per-Migration Test Coverage
